A brief tornado occurred over northern rural Osceola County on Monday, August 4, 2025 as confirmed by a combination of video evidence from local media partners and data from the National Weather Service Melbourne (KMLB) radar. 

The tornado developed as a result of numerous low-level boundary collisions. The circulation is estimated to have touched down at approximately 7:14 PM EDT along the southern side of Lake Joel in St. Cloud, near Sungrove Ln and the C-32 Canal. KMLB radar data indicate the circulation, along with a corresponding debris signature, moved east over a densely wooded area before subsequently lifting around 7:22 PM EDT., just west of Storey Bend Rd. 

Given limited access to the affected area, the track is considered approximate, and an EF-rating cannot be provided at this time. Refinements to the track will be made if additional photographic or video evidence becomes available.

Both homes suffered complete destruction, with debris blown away from the foundation. Current estimated wind speed is a consensus.

properties.dod_txt: Destruction of engineered and/or well constructed residence; slab swept clean
properties.comments: Two story house on cinder block foundation. Not well attached. Tornado appeared to move ESE onto property. House was swept to the north northeast in the radial flow toward the center of the vortex. Based on surrounding context of tree damage, was likely right on the fringe of the tornado core. Exceptional tree damage just north of the house. Ground scouring evident on property. Update 5/15: Wind speed increased to 180 mph based on combination of house swept off its foundation and multiple elements of nearby tree damage. Bald cypress tree adjacent to NW corner of the house was pulled from the ground, with the largest fragment found in the field 120 yards to the SE. Large black walnut tree to the NE of the house was snapped about 5-6 ft from the base and thrown 50 ft. Both trees were stripped of all leaves and minor branches and partially or mostly debarked. Evidence of numerous other trees farther back on property also having been bodily removed from the ground and thrown significant distances. Large oaks and osage orange trees were also stripped of even their largest limbs. Two large tanks were displaced, with one moved over 300 yards from its starting location.

properties.comments:
A survey team found the damage to Central Elementary School in 
Steele, MO, was associated with straight-line winds. A 
significant portion of the roof of one of the school buildings was removed and blown to the east. Numerous small branches and 
several larger tree limbs were downed adjacent to the school and nearby park. Damage patterns and a review of security footage were consistent with straight-line wind damage, likely associated with a microburst. No additional damage was noted in the area. Maximum estimated wind speeds were 80 mph.

At the bottom of the hill there is concentrated microburst damage. Impressive damage extent with hundreds and hundreds of snapped trees down. No visible wind damage to structures.
This marks the southern edge of Cow Island microburst damage. I know of at least 30 to 50 trees down all falling in a general east and northeast direction.
Visible damage begins again at Tuftonboro Neck. No visible damage to the Backlands of Cow Island. This is likely a second microburst starting point.
Northern Edge of second microburst area with a general east northeast fall direction, Hundreds of snapped Eastern White Pines.
Driftwood Cove Road intersection walking down towards lakefront there was widespread microburst damage approximately 1000 trees down in this region.

This is the southern edge of damage extent. It was near this point that trees fell on a small boat launch building where people were sheltering. Several cuts/scrapes. One person was injured on the hand when a tree fell on their car in the parking lot nearby, but they refused treatment.
Mixed forest blow down marking the northern edge of second microburst at Camp Northwood. Hundreds of trees down in a similar east northeast direction.
Two cabins destroyed and many others slightly damaged due to falling trees. In the center of the damage at this point, mix of hardwood and soft wood uprooted and snapped.
Continued significant tree damage, including a few more destroyed buildings.
Significant damage on the lakefront.  Two more destroyed structures, one bunkhouse and one bath house. Both were caused by tree falls.
Three destroyed cabins and another one damaged.  All were due to tree strikes. Also close to the edge of the concentrated wind damage near the lakefront.

properties.comments:
Along Highway 12/Cedar Island Road, just east of the Thorofare
Bridge, two cedar trees were snapped up from the base of the
trunk. The trees were on the smaller side and an average between
the expected values for large branches broken but below trunks
snapped were used to account for this. With extensive marshland in
this area, the wind estimate was quite difficult with no other
trees or buildings to determine a threshold of damage. Powerlines
along this road are metal and have a high wind threshold. They did
not exhibit any damage. Eyewitnesses reported a waterspout cross
Highway 12 (Cedar Island Road) at the same time the radar showed
an intense area of rotation just above the surface. A path width
could not be determined due to the extensive marshland and lack of
other areas of damage. Confidence is high in the determination of
a tornado based on the combination of strong radar evidence and
eyewitness accounts that match the exact location damage was
found. Wind estimate confidence is a bit lower than usual given
the lack of any trees or buildings in that area to make a more
conclusive determination of wind speed. An estimation of top wind
speeds between 75 and 85 MPH is reasonable given the exhibited
damage.

It should be noted that pictures of a funnel cloud and potential
tornado were circulated on social media about the same time the 
tornado above occurred. These pictures however are likely from a 
separate funnel cloud or tornado. The location of where the 
pictures were taken was in Bettie, NC, along highway 70. This was 
16 miles to the southwest of the storm survey location above. In 
addition the tornado surveyed was likely rain wrapped and would 
not be visible from that distance. We have not received any damage
reports associated with this possible second funnel cloud or 
tornado, despite reaching out to Open Ground Farms. If additional 
information comes into the office, a second survey or additional 
information will be sent out.

25x70 car port lifted over a house and onto a power line. Some sheet metal thrown about 50 yards to the northeast. The carport had an open wall facing south-southwest.
